## Hinge question · Count and sum {#ss2-hinge .sequence-hinge .sigma-hinge}

```{=html}
<div data-module="hinge" data-correct="2" class="hinge numeric-choices">
<p class="hinge-question">For <span data-math="\displaystyle\sum_{k=2}^{5}(2k-1)">the sum from k = 2 to 5 of (2k − 1)</span>, which statement is correct?</p>
<div class="hinge-toolbar"><div class="time" role="timer" aria-label="Time remaining">1:00</div><div class="toolbar"><label>Seconds <select class="timer-duration" aria-label="Question duration"><option>30</option><option>45</option><option selected>60</option><option>90</option><option>120</option></select></label><button class="timer-start primary">Start</button><button class="reset-question">Reset</button></div></div>
<div class="choices">
<button class="choice" data-answer="1" aria-pressed="false"><b>1</b><span>5 terms, with sum 25.</span></button>
<button class="choice" data-answer="2" aria-pressed="false"><b>2</b><span>4 terms, with sum 24.</span></button>
<button class="choice" data-answer="3" aria-pressed="false"><b>3</b><span>3 terms, with sum 15.</span></button>
<button class="choice" data-answer="4" aria-pressed="false"><b>4</b><span>4 terms, with sum 9.</span></button>
</div>
<div class="hinge-bottom"><p>Fist on chest. Think quietly.<br>On “show”, hold up 1–4 fingers.</p><button class="reveal-answer primary">Reveal answer</button></div>
<div class="hinge-explanation" hidden><strong>2.</strong> Indices <span data-math="2,3,4,5">2, 3, 4, 5</span> give four terms.<br><span data-math="3+5+7+9=24">3 + 5 + 7 + 9 = 24</span>.</div>
</div>
```

::: notes
Default 60 seconds. Fist on chest, quiet thinking, then everyone shows 1–4 fingers simultaneously on the teacher's verbal cue. Timer expiry never reveals the answer. Collect responses before the separate answer reveal.

1: Starts at k=1, producing 1+3+5+7+9=25 and five terms.
2 (correct): k=2,3,4,5 produces 3+5+7+9=24 and four terms.
3: Excludes the upper endpoint, producing 3+5+7=15 and three terms.
4: Counts the indices correctly but reports the last term, 2(5)−1=9, as the sum.

Ready: ask students to explain why the lower limit changes both the count and the sum, then proceed.
Divided: have pairs compare their lists of indices and re-poll before revealing.
Reteach: write the index row 2,3,4,5, then the value row 3,5,7,9. Recheck the count and sum separately.
:::
